note: Sits on the edge/outside boundary and is recorded as edge because two criteria hold firmly. Successful holds on the 'or equivalent' clause — a cyber security engineer in a role he describes as having 'a lot of long-term prospects' is a credible professional equivalent, though not the business-owner or physician profile the quote names. Not deconditioned holds emphatically on the exclusion as written: the exclusion is being fifty pounds overweight AND gym-averse, and he is the opposite of gym-averse, training four to six days a week without missing a week in a long time. Income is the decisive miss and it is unambiguous: 'I definitely wouldn't be able to pay it up front', 'I've only got a very little amount of savings', 'my last kind of 10 years have been very complicated financially', and finally 'I can't warrant that money.' Neglected health fails for the same reason it failed for Brent — health is the area he already manages hardest, not the one he has let slide. Good-to-great is the borderline call: at 100 kg and 5'6" with 'a fair amount of body fat' and a self-rating of five out of ten, he is closer to the rescue end than the refinement end, and his stated driver is escaping a former self rather than exceeding a current one. Two observations for the rollup. First, this is the second consecutive prospect in this batch whose health is not neglected, which suggests the lead source is delivering already-training buyers the stated ICP does not describe. Second, the stated ICP again has no clinical criterion, and this prospect disclosed an acromioclavicular separation, recurrent shoulder and elbow problems and a diagnosed hamstring dysfunction that no ICP test would surface.
